title: UL1 Unseen: typing on while a reply is prepared, and a Provider that never answers
capability: Second, unseen counterpart of the request-lifecycle case, run with the real model and the product's default request budget. While a reply is still being prepared the person keeps typing: the newer message is taken as an addition, the older reply is never shown and never stored. A reply whose Provider does not answer is stopped at the 60 second request deadline with an honest timeout, commits nothing late and leaves nothing running, and the conversation carries on normally afterwards. The stalled Provider is an injected fault; that request is never sent to the real Provider.

allowed.statement: The person's young niece came along to the temple fair, and the two of them shared a stick of candied fruit sitting on stone steps beside the stage.

forbidden.statement: Explaining the delay or the stopped request in system terms such as timeouts, streams or retries.
Going on about the plan to fly a kite by the river when only the companion was asked for.

expectedBehavior: The addition is answered as asked: who came along.
The stalled request ends by itself at the deadline and leaves nothing behind.
The next message is answered normally.
failureSignals: The replaced reply is shown or stored.
The stalled request runs past the deadline, or commits afterwards.

sourceEligibility.reason: Retained original expression; names the companion.
Retained original expression of the plan.

criteria.description: The reply to the replaced question is neither shown nor stored.
History holds the addition once, followed by exactly its reply.
The replaced question still reaches the Provider with the addition.
The message naming the companion reaches the Provider.
With the product's own budget, a request whose Provider never answers ends with a timeout by 60 seconds (61 allowed for the client to see it), commits nothing late and leaves nothing running.
The next message is answered normally.
The addition is answered as asked, in ordinary words.
